claim_review_spans.R1: That is a genuinely stressful situation to deal with, especially when you are balancing classes and a ticking clock. To answer your first question directly: **No, you should not tell your dad it is handled and wait.** An automatic reply from a university email account only means your message was received, not that a staff member has reviewed it or that your deadline is extended. And your classmate is right to be worried about a registration hold, though a minor payment delay doesn't automatically mean losing your visa status today.
claim_review_spans.R2: The biggest red flag here—and the likely reason for the "verification pending"—is that **the payment was made using your old applicant number instead of your current student number.** Because the university's automated system doesn't know who to match that money to, it is sitting in a holding account while your student account still shows as unpaid.
claim_review_spans.R3: Here is what you should do **first**, before 5 p.m. today:
claim_review_spans.R4: If your dad recalls the wire transfer now, it could take days or weeks for the funds to return to his account, and you *would* risk getting a severe registration hold in the meantime. Instead, you need to link the money that is *already* moving to your correct student number.
claim_review_spans.R5: Since you already emailed them, send a follow-up reply to that same thread right now. Make the subject line impossible to ignore, and explicitly point out the wrong number.
claim_review_spans.R6: You can adapt and send this email right away:
claim_review_spans.R7: **Subject:** URGENT: Tuition Payment ID Correction – [Your Full Name] – [Your Student ID Number]
claim_review_spans.R8: I am writing to follow up on my previous email regarding my tuition payment deadline today at 5:00 p.m.
claim_review_spans.R9: My family initiated the wire transfer last week, but I realized that the payment request unfortunately used my old applicant number (**[Insert Old Applicant Number]**) instead of my current student ID number (**[Insert Your Current Student ID Number]**).
claim_review_spans.R10: Attached is the completed receipt from the payment service showing the transfer. The funds have left our bank. Could you please manually apply this payment to my current student account (**[Insert Your Current Student ID Number]**) to clear the balance before the 5 p.m. deadline?
claim_review_spans.R11: Thank you for your help, and please let me know if you need any additional information.
claim_review_spans.R13: If your campus has a physical Student Accounts or Bursar's office, **do not rely on email alone today.** Print out the bank receipt showing the money left your account, your passport, and your student ID card. Walk into the office before 4 p.m., show them the paperwork, and explain: *"The money was sent last week, but my applicant number was used instead of my student number by mistake. Can you place a temporary note on my account so I avoid a hold while it is sorted?"* Face-to-face contact usually stops automated holds instantly.
claim_review_spans.R14: Let your dad know *not* to recall the wire yet. Tell him the bank's "completed" status combined with the receipt is your proof, but the university just needs to manually match the old applicant number to your new student number. Ask him to send you any "payer ID document" the payment service requested as soon as he is free after 6 p.m., just in case the university's third-party payment portal needs it to clear the verification on their end.
claim_review_spans.R15: Take a deep breath. Administrative mix-ups with applicant versus student numbers happen to international students all the time at the start of the term. Getting your ID number corrected in writing and in person is your fastest fix.

claim_review_spans.R1: Take a deep breath. Stop right there—do not take the medicine yet, and do not guess.
claim_review_spans.R2: Here is what you need to know and do right now while you are standing at that pharmacy counter:
claim_review_spans.R3: **Do not take the medicine yet.** A prescription that says "as needed" means you only take it when symptoms arise (like pain or nausea), whereas "every day" means a strict schedule. Taking them incorrectly can be dangerous.
claim_review_spans.R4: The most important fact is: **That sign is right in front of you, and phone interpreters are free.** You do not need to use your roommate, and you do not need to fake understanding.
claim_review_spans.R5: > *"I am an international student, and I am very confused by these instructions. Can we please use your free phone interpreter service right now to clarify how to take this?"*
claim_review_spans.R6: **Do not try to change the past record by saying an interpreter wasn't available.** Doing so creates a false official record, which can cause serious complications with future medical care, insurance, or liability if something goes wrong.
claim_review_spans.R7: Instead, you can fix the record the right way *tomorrow*: Call the clinic's patient relations or main desk, or send a message through their online portal, and simply state: *"I want to add a note to my visit record from [Date]. I declined the interpreter at check-in because of a misunderstanding about costs, but I actually need language assistance for all future appointments."* Clinics deal with this all the time; they add an addendum, which protects you safely and honestly.
claim_review_spans.R8: Your roommate means well, but managing coursework in English is completely different from understanding complex medical dosage instructions.
claim_review_spans.R10: > *"Thanks for waiting, but the pharmacy instructions are complicated and I'm using the clinic's free interpreter service to sort it out with the pharmacist. It'll just take a few extra minutes!"*
claim_review_spans.R11: **Your immediate step:** Turn to the pharmacist, point to the free interpreter sign, and ask them to connect you to a phone interpreter before you leave that counter.

claim_review_spans.R1: It is completely understandable that you are feeling ashamed and confused right now. You wanted to show genuine appreciation for the extra help your instructor gave you, you followed what you thought the rules were, and having a gift returned can feel very personal and embarrassing—especially when you are a first-year student far from home and navigating a brand-new academic culture.
claim_review_spans.R2: To help untangle this, let's look at what is likely happening, separate the cultural differences from the rules, and figure out your next steps.
claim_review_spans.R3: 1. **The Timing Issue (The Core Problem):** Even though a department email said gifts are generally fine *after* final marks are recorded, your semester is just beginning and your first assignment is still being graded. In many U.S. universities, instructors are strictly prohibited from accepting *anything* of material value from a current student while that student's grade is actively being determined. It creates an ethical conflict—or even the appearance of trying to influence a grade—regardless of your pure intentions.
claim_review_spans.R4: 2. **The Card vs. The Gift:** The instructor kept the card because a handwritten note expressing gratitude is universally appreciated and entirely appropriate. They returned the physical gift not because they dislike you or your culture, but to protect themselves and maintain strict professional boundaries while grading your work.
claim_review_spans.R5: 3. **The Graduation Photo:** You mentioned seeing a photo of the instructor accepting flowers at graduation. That is a completely different context: the student had already graduated and final marks were locked in, so there was no conflict of interest.
claim_review_spans.R6: 4. **Your Parents' Perspective:** Your parents are viewing this through the lens of hospitality and respect common in many cultures, where refusing a gift is considered a serious social rejection. That cultural mismatch makes the situation hurt much more than it would otherwise.
claim_review_spans.R7: **Do not insist, and do not leave the gift anonymously in the mailbox.**
claim_review_spans.R8: Quoting the email or leaving the gift secretly will likely make the instructor uncomfortable and could unnecessarily complicate your relationship with them. Your friend's advice here could backfire.
claim_review_spans.R9: At the same time, **do not stay away.** Your instructor explicitly wrote, *"You're welcome at office hours tomorrow."* This is a very positive sign. It means the instructor understands you made a cultural or timing mistake, holds no ill will toward you, and wants to help you with your course question. In U.S. academia, strict boundary-setting does not mean the person hates you; it just means they follow institutional rules very carefully.
claim_review_spans.R10: Go to office hours for your course question. You can briefly and calmly clear the air, which will help relieve your shame. You do not need to over-explain or defend yourself.
claim_review_spans.R11: Here is a short, simple script you can use when you walk in:
claim_review_spans.R12: > *"Hi [Instructor's Last Name], thank you for having me. Before we look at my course question, I just wanted to say thank you for your note, and I understand why you returned the gift. I'm still learning how things work here, and I appreciate you setting that straight."*
claim_review_spans.R13: Then, transition directly to your academic question. Once you do that, the awkwardness will instantly dissolve.
claim_review_spans.R14: When talking to your parents, it helps to frame it around *institutional compliance* rather than personal rejection, reassuring them that you are safe and respected. You might tell them:
claim_review_spans.R15: > *"I was embarrassed at first, but I've learned that American universities have very strict anti-corruption rules for professors. Even though the department allows gifts after grades are final, professors cannot accept anything while they are actively grading a student's work, to keep things completely fair. It wasn't a rejection of our culture or our gratitude—it was just the professor following strict professional rules to protect their job. They kept my thank-you card, and everything is fine with my classes."*
claim_review_spans.R16: How are you feeling about going to office hours tomorrow? Do you feel ready to drop off the gift issue and focus on your coursework, or is the shame still making it hard to think about going?

claim_review_spans.R1: This is a very stressful situation, especially when you are just a few weeks into your first semester. Take a breath: **you have not failed, and you have not lost your work.** You have the original PDF from 10:56 and your handwritten answers, which means your work physically exists.
claim_review_spans.R2: However, **do not follow your friend's advice to rename or alter the file's date.** Altering metadata or modifying a file after a deadline can trigger an academic integrity investigation, which is a much bigger hurdle to clear than a technical submission glitch.
claim_review_spans.R3: You have a very tight deadline—noon today—so let's focus strictly on what you need to do right now.
claim_review_spans.R4: 1. **Submit the official Exam Review form immediately.** Do not wait for IT or for tomorrow. The university's official policy explicitly requires you to use this form by noon.
claim_review_spans.R5: 2. **Do not tidy the scan or change any files.** Leave the 10:56 PDF exactly as it is.
claim_review_spans.R6: 3. **Draft a clear, factual message.** State what happened without panicking or over-explaining.
claim_review_spans.R7: Here is a template you can adapt and submit through the Exam Review form right now:
claim_review_spans.R8: **Subject:** Urgent: Technical submission error / Exam Review Request – [Your Name] – [Course Name]
claim_review_spans.R9: The exam window closed at 11:00 a.m. At 10:58 a.m., I uploaded my exam file. The internet connection froze momentarily, but the system displayed "submission received" at 10:59 a.m.
claim_review_spans.R10: When I checked the gradebook today, I saw the placeholder grade and downloaded my submission to verify it. Unfortunately, only the cover page uploaded successfully due to the freeze.
claim_review_spans.R11: My complete, unedited exam PDF (created and last modified at 10:56 a.m. yesterday, prior to submission) and my original handwritten working notes are fully intact on my computer. I have attached the complete 10-page PDF to this request for your review. I have also opened an IT ticket ([Insert IT ticket number if you have one]).
claim_review_spans.R12: I kindly request that my complete file be accepted for grading, or that I be given guidance on how to submit the correct file. Thank you for your time and understanding.
claim_review_spans.R13: * **Attach the 10-page PDF** and your IT ticket confirmation (if available) directly to that form.
claim_review_spans.R14: * **Keep your handwritten notes safe.** Do not throw them away or alter them.
claim_review_spans.R15: You ran into a frustrating technical glitch, which happens to students at all levels, not just first-year international students. It is a procedural problem with a clear paper trail, not a reflection of your ability to handle university.
claim_review_spans.R16: Go ahead and submit that form now while you have the time. How are you feeling about getting that form sent in before the noon deadline?

claim_review_spans.R1: It is completely understandable that you agreed out of fear and pressure. When you have only been in a new country for a few weeks, your first close friend feels like a lifeline, and the thought of losing that support is terrifying.
claim_review_spans.R2: To answer your question directly: **No, keeping this promise is not a path to making things normal.**
claim_review_spans.R3: What Ari is asking for—constant availability, tracking your location all evening, and demanding proof of who you are with—is not how healthy friendships work. If you give in tonight, it establishes a precedent that surveillance and emotional pressure are the price of their friendship. The demands will likely increase, not stop.
claim_review_spans.R4: Since you want to salvage the friendship if possible *while* protecting your boundaries, here is a way to handle tonight and what you should watch for moving forward.
claim_review_spans.R5: You need to revoke the location-sharing condition without starting an explosive fight, but you must be clear. You do not need to send a group photo or keep your location on.
claim_review_spans.R6: You can adapt and send a text like this:
claim_review_spans.R7: > *"Hey Ari, I’m glad we talked earlier and I appreciate your apology. But after thinking about it, I realize that keeping my location on all evening and sending photos doesn't feel right for me. I'm going to dinner with my classmates, but I won't be sharing my live location. I value our friendship and I'll text you tomorrow when I'm back."*
claim_review_spans.R8: **If they blow up or send a flurry of messages:** Put your phone on "Do Not Disturb" and go to your dinner. You do not have to answer them instantly.
claim_review_spans.R9: Pay close attention to how Ari reacts over the next few days. Healthy people make mistakes, apologize, and accept boundaries when given some space. Look out for these warning signs of controlling behavior:
claim_review_spans.R10: * **The "Guilt Trip":** Reminding you constantly of how much they helped you with your phone plan and groceries, framing you as "ungrateful." (Help is a gift, not a debt that buys control over your life).
claim_review_spans.R11: * **The Silent Treatment or Punnishment:** Withdrawing communication to punish you for going to dinner.
claim_review_spans.R12: * **Escalation:** Demanding even tighter control over your schedule or other friendships.
claim_review_spans.R13: Ari was your first friend, which makes them very important right now, but relying on just *one* person for your social life and practical help puts you in a very vulnerable position.
claim_review_spans.R14: Over the next couple of weeks, try to lean a little more into connections with your classmates, people in your dorm or housing, or campus international student groups. The more you realize that other people are kind, welcoming, and won't demand to track your movements, the less power Ari's pressure will hold over you.
claim_review_spans.R15: How are you feeling about going to dinner with your classmates tonight? Do you need help figuring out how to set a phone boundary so you can actually enjoy your evening?
